Abstract.AbstractText: hNav1.7 receives a lot of attention owing to its attractive mechanism of action in pain processing pathway. We have previously reported our design of a novel series of tetrahydropyridine analogues towards hNav1.7 selective inhibitors. Herein, we disclose further efforts to the optimization of hit compound (-)-6, which led to the identification of aminocyclohexene analogues (-)-9 and (-)-17 with good potency, high selectivity, and minimal CYP inhibition. Both compounds (-)-9 and (-)-17 demonstrated improved pharmacokinetic profiles in rats, and robust efficacy in rat formalin-induced nociception and spinal nerve ligation (SNL) models.
